subject: Post-demo: Stakeholder map & decision criteria (latency / cost / SLA) - Finova
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Stakeholder map & decision criteria (latency / cost / SLA) - Finova

Hi Sarah 1

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Great to learn more about Finova's use case for real-time assistant capabilities in the customer support flow. Quick recap and next steps to make sure we map stakeholders and decision criteria correctly: 

1) Decision criteria we heard on the call:
   - Latency: p95 generation target <= 250ms for single-turn customer replies (goal) / acceptable up to 400ms for certain journeys.
   - Cost: target cost per 1k messages to be under $X (we'll confirm exact number with your finance team) 1 core ask is keeping monthly token spend predictable.
   - Deployment mode: preference for Dedicated / VPC deployment for data isolation; open to Hosted if we can meet security requirements and SLA.
   - SLA: uptime and latency SLOs required for production (we noted 99.9% for customer-facing endpoints).

2) Stakeholder map (from today's attendees + suggested additions):
   - Economic buyer: Evan Morales (VP Product) 1 controls budget and renewal.
   - Procurement / Legal: procurement@finova.com + legal counsel (TBD) 1 will own contract/terms and SOC 2 evidence requests.
   - Security & Compliance: likely a security contact (please confirm name) 1 will need SOC 2, data retention, KMS/HSM details.
   - Engineering / Platform: Sarah + engineering lead for integration and rollout planning.

3) Ask from our side:
   - Can you confirm the economic buyer and procurement contact?
   - Is the latency target above (p95 <=250ms, acceptable <=400ms) accurate for the primary customer flow?
   - Any hard constraints on deployment (must be VPC/on-prem) or is Dedicated with private networking sufficient?

4) Next steps proposed:
   - Ill share the demo recording and a short one-pager mapping how Redwood meets the latency/SLA targets across Hosted vs Dedicated. (attached)
   - Wed like to schedule a 30-min follow-up with Evan + procurement to go over pricing and procurement timelines 1 available next week Wed/Thu.

Attachments: 20260226-demo-recording.mp4 (recording), SOW-draft-v1.pdf (outline)

Thanks 1 appreciate a quick confirmation of the stakeholder contacts and the latency/cost constraints so we can prepare the right materials for procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stakeholder map & decision criteria (latency / cost / SLA) - Finova

Hi Marissa 1

Thanks for the recap and recording. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: 250ms p95 is our target for quick chat responses in the live support channel. We can accept up to 350-400ms for async follow-ups (e.g., email summarization).
- Cost: the finance team wants an estimated monthly spend range based on ~150k messages/month (we'll provide more detailed traffic patterns by next week).
- Deployment: VP Product (Evan) prefers Dedicated in our cloud account with private networking; security will likely require an SOC 2 attestation and KMS integration. On-prem is only considered for regulated workloads later.

Evan is looping in procurement (procurement@finova.com) 1 Evan, can you confirm the procurement POC and timeline?

Sarah
Product Lead, Finova

Hi Evan / Sarah / Lina 1

Thanks for confirming procurement POC Lina 1 great to meet you. Quick reply with attachments and next steps below.

What Ive attached to help procurement / security:
- SOW-draft-v1.pdf  high-level scope and optional Dedicated pricing bands (ballpark ranges)
- 20260226-demo-recording.mp4  demo recording
- Link to our security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/SOC2 (SOC 2 + KMS integration doc)

Short answers to the asks:
- SOC 2 & security: We will share current SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; our private deployments support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK) and HSM integrations for key custody.
- Latency p95: For Dedicated we provision GPU pools and tune kernel selection + batching to meet p95 targets. Typical p95 for Redwood Dedicated for similar workloads is 120-220ms depending on prompt size and model; we include automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant if a node is saturated to preserve p95. I can add a short appendix with profiling numbers based on your expected prompt lengths.
- Pricing sketch: in the attached SOW draft we list three bands for Dedicated monthly commit; I'll follow up with a hosted estimate for 150k messages once we get the tokenization assumptions from your team.

Proposed next steps:
- Lina/procurement: we can set a 30-min kickoff this Thu 11:00 or Fri 14:00 PT  which works?
- Evan: Would you like a short appendix with p95 profiling for the exact prompt examples you mentioned? If yes, please drop 3 representative prompts and average token lengths.

If helpful, I can also put together a one-page decision criteria checklist (latency / cost / security / deployment) for your stakeholders to circulate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
